title: Project backlog and product backlog
blurb: Tell the project backlog from a team's product backlog: what each replaces, what it holds, who owns it and how changes to it are handled.
question: A project has three delivery teams. Which backlog holds the high-level epics for the whole project and who owns it, and which backlog does each team work from?

teach.body: A backlog is a prioritized list of the requirements for a product, written as (epic) user stories or other requirement formats. PRINCE2 Agile uses backlogs at two levels. The project backlog describes what the whole project must deliver. Each delivery team then works from its own product backlog, with the detail that team needs.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Glossary and 8.3.2.1

teach.body: The project backlog is PRINCE2 Agile's tailoring of the project product description. It usually holds high-level requirements as epic user stories, shows or links to the project Definition of Ready and Definition of Done from the quality management approach, and names who accepts the project product. It is first created in starting up a project, and the project manager checks whether it needs updating when preparing the project plan.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3.2.1; Tables 13.1 and 13.6

teach.body: A product backlog contains everything a regular backlog does, and it also includes or links to the team Definition of Done. It is used at team level by the person responsible for the team's outputs: the product owner. It holds the detailed user stories, with the information the team needs, and replaces product descriptions.

teach.h: Who does what with the backlogs
head: Role
Backlog responsibility
rows: Owns the project backlog; sets priorities across teams
Owns one team's product backlog; keeps it aligned
Consults POs and stakeholders on product backlogs
Refines the product backlog in team planning

teach.h: Does the change alter the approved scope in the project backlog?

children.label: Baseline change
children.sub: Formal: project board or delegated change authority

children.label: Detail change
children.sub: Informal: handled at team level with the PO

teach.body: Brackenfield is moving parking permits online. Chief product owner Hannah Okafor owns the project backlog, with epics such as 'apply for a resident permit' and 'manage visitor permits'. Product owner Daniel Reyes owns the resident permits team's product backlog, holding detailed stories and the team's Definition of Done. Adding a new business permit type as a Must-have would change the approved project backlog, so it goes to the board. Rewording a form field does not, so Daniel's team handles it.

teach.text: The chief product owner owns the project backlog and prioritizes across teams; each product owner owns one team's product backlog. The project backlog replaces the project product description, not the project plan (that is the release map). The team Definition of Done sits with the product backlog; the project DoR and DoD sit with the project backlog.

items: Backlog: a prioritized list of requirements for a product.
Project backlog replaces the project product description; mostly epics.
It shows or links to the project DoR and DoD and names the acceptor.
Product backlog replaces product descriptions and links the team DoD.
CPO owns the project backlog; each PO owns a team's product backlog.
A new or changed Must-have in the project backlog is a baseline change, handled formally.

summary: You can now tell the project backlog (epics, owned by the chief product owner, replacing the project product description) from each team's product backlog (detailed stories, owned by a product owner). You can also explain why a change to the approved scope in the project backlog is handled formally.

A.q: Which management product does the project backlog replace in PRINCE2 Agile?
options: The project plan and stage plans
A.why: The project backlog is tailored to replace the contents of the project product description (8.3.2.1).

whyNot.1: Project and stage plans are represented by the release map.
whyNot.2: The business case is tailored into the project canvas.
whyNot.3: A work package description becomes a set of user stories.

A.q: Which role owns the project backlog?
A.why: The CPO owns the project backlog, keeps it refined with user input and aligned with team product backlogs (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: A product owner owns one team's product backlog, not the project backlog.
whyNot.1: The project manager consults on backlogs but does not own the project backlog.
whyNot.2: The executive is accountable for the project; backlog ownership sits with the CPO.

A.q: Which role owns a delivery team's product backlog?
A.why: The product owner owns the product backlog and keeps it aligned with the project backlog (Table 7.2, 8.3.2.1).

whyNot.0: The CPO owns the project backlog and prioritizes across teams.
whyNot.2: The team coach helps the team self-manage and write stories but does not own the backlog.
whyNot.3: Project support gives administrative help; it does not own any backlog.

B.q:
Which two statements about backlogs in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?
1. A product backlog includes or links to the team Definition of Done.
2. The project backlog mainly holds detailed task lists.
3. The project backlog names who accepts the project product.
4. The product owner sets priorities across all teams.
B.why: Statements 1 and 3 match 8.3.2.1. The project backlog holds mostly epics, and the CPO prioritizes across teams.

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: the project backlog usually holds high-level epics, not tasks.
whyNot.2: Both are false: the project backlog is high level, and prioritizing across teams is the CPO's job.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the PO looks after one team's backlog.

B.q: Which backlog should show or link to the project Definition of Ready and Definition of Done?
B.why: The project backlog shows or links to the project DoR and DoD from the quality management approach (8.3.2.1).

whyNot.0: The product backlog links to the team Definition of Done, not the project-level ones.
whyNot.1: A risk-adjusted backlog combines stories and risk responses in a product backlog (risk practice).
whyNot.3: The team plan sets out tasks for the next iteration; it does not carry the project DoR and DoD.

B.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. A [?] backlog is used at team level by the person responsible for the team's outputs.
B.why: Product backlogs are used at team level by the person responsible for the team's outputs, the product owner (8.3.2.1).

whyNot.1: The project backlog covers the whole project and is owned by the CPO.
whyNot.2: PRINCE2 Agile plans releases on a release map; it does not use a 'release backlog'.
whyNot.3: 'Sprint backlog' is a Scrum term; PRINCE2 Agile uses the product backlog and team plan.

C.q: A proposed new Must-have requirement would change the approved project backlog. How is it handled, and who decides?
options: Informally, by the PO at team level
Formally, by the PO and the team coach
Informally, by the CPO in team planning
Formally, by the board or change authority
C.why: A new Must-have that changes the approved project backlog is a change to the project baseline, handled formally by the board or those with delegated change authority (11.3.2).

whyNot.0: Team-level informal handling applies to detail changes that leave the project backlog unchanged.
whyNot.1: The handling is formal, but the PO and team coach are not the change authority.
whyNot.2: A baseline change is not settled informally in a team workshop.

C.q: Which role keeps the project backlog aligned with the team product backlogs, and whom does that role represent?
C.why: The CPO represents the user community, owns the project backlog and keeps it aligned with the team product backlogs (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: The PO looks after one team's backlog; the supplier side is represented by the senior supplier.
whyNot.1: The PM runs the project day to day for the board but does not own the project backlog.
whyNot.3: The role is right but the CPO represents users, not the delivery teams.

C.q: Which item is MOST LIKELY to appear in the project backlog rather than a product backlog?
options: An epic user story for the whole service
Detailed stories with team acceptance criteria
A link to the team Definition of Done
The tasks planned for the next iteration
C.why: The project backlog usually holds high-level requirements as epic user stories (8.3.2.1).

whyNot.1: Detailed, team-ready stories belong in a product backlog.
whyNot.2: The team DoD is included in or linked from the product backlog.
whyNot.3: Next-iteration tasks belong in the team plan.

reteach.title: One shopping list, several trolleys
reteach.question: When a family splits a big shopping list between three people, who keeps the master list, and what does each person carry?

blocks.body: The project backlog is the master list: big items (epics) for the whole project, owned by the chief product owner. Each team has its own list, the product backlog, broken into detailed stories and owned by its product owner. Changing the approved must-haves on the master list needs the board's say; adjusting a team list within it does not.

blocks.text: CPO = project backlog, across teams. PO = product backlog, one team.

explain.body: A backlog is a prioritized list of requirements for a product, written as (epic) user stories or other formats.

test.q: Which statement BEST describes a backlog in PRINCE2 Agile?
options: A log of risks raised by the team
A list of tasks for one iteration
A record of completed quality checks
test.why: A backlog is a prioritized list of the requirements for a product (Glossary).

whyNot.0: Risks are recorded in the risk register.
whyNot.1: Tasks for one iteration are in the team plan.
whyNot.2: Completed quality activities are recorded in the quality register.

explain.body: Mostly epics; shows or links to the project DoR and DoD; names who accepts the project product.

test.q: Which detail should the project backlog mention?
test.why: The project backlog names the individuals or roles responsible for accepting the project product (8.3.2.1).

whyNot.0: Coaching arrangements belong to the organization practice, not the project backlog.
whyNot.2: Tasks are planned by the team in the team plan.
whyNot.3: Tools and working arrangements sit in the project management team structure.

explain.body: Everything a regular backlog has, plus the team Definition of Done; used by the product owner at team level.

test.q: Beyond a regular backlog, what should a product backlog include or link to?
test.why: A PRINCE2 Agile product backlog includes or links to the team DoD (8.3.2.1).

whyNot.0: The project canvas is the business case artifact.
whyNot.1: The delegation matrix shows decision authority in the organization practice.
whyNot.3: The project DoR is shown or linked in the project backlog, not the product backlog.

explain.body: If a change alters the approved scope in the project backlog, such as a new Must-have, it is a baseline change, handled formally. If it does not affect the project backlog, it is a detail change, handled at team level.

test.q: A change clarifies a user story but does not affect the project backlog. What type of change is it?
test.why: A change that does not affect the project backlog is a detail change, handled informally at team level (11.3.2).

whyNot.0: A baseline change alters the project backlog.
whyNot.2: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its specification.
whyNot.3: An exception is a forecast breach of tolerance.
